title: Dump Management
body: Run two dump projects at once without a clear priority call and you end up with an unfinished fill sitting half-done for weeks — bad for auditors, and a magnet for equipment straying into an area that was supposed to be closed out.
keyPoints: When two dump/fill jobs are live at once, finish the short, nearly-complete one before committing to the long one. A 2-3 day job left open while a month-long job grinds on looks worse on audit than a job that hasn't started yet.
The moment you pause work on any dump section, lock it down physically — cones, drums, tape — so equipment doesn't drift into the incomplete corner while attention is elsewhere.

New dump ramps get built top-down. The upper section has to be substantially complete before the next section opens, and a single-lane ramp needs widening before you can scale dumping volume through it.
Confirm the offset/limit boundary line is actually set and communicated before you shift crew priority between elevations — that's what lets one dump pause without blocking work on another.
apply: If North Dump or Northwest Dump work comes up on shift, check whether the paused 950-fill corner still has its physical controls in place before anyone assumes it's clear to drive through.
